name: Maximum Positive Degree
definition: The **Maximum Positive Degree** of a concept class is the maximum dominance of its $1$-inclusion graph (where dominance is the number of neighbors that are smaller with respect to inclusion).
comments: Conditioning gives an induced subgraph of the oriented $1$-inclusion graph and preserves the inclusion orientation, so maximum positive degree cannot increase.

monotonic.proof: Adding concepts can only add lower one-inclusion neighbours to existing concepts and introduces one additional nonnegative positive degree. Hence the maximum positive degree cannot decrease under inclusion of classes.

p_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: H={01,10} has no oriented one-inclusion edge, hence maximum positive degree 0. Projecting to either coordinate gives {0,1}, whose top vertex has one lower neighbour, so the value is 1.

c_monotonic.proof: After fixing the conditioned labels, the oriented one-inclusion graph of the fibre is an induced oriented subgraph, so maximum positive degree cannot increase.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.
